land.text: all of the Karkota kingdom: 'Founded by Avantivarman in 855, it replaced the Karkota dynasty'

predecessors.note: Karkota dossier: 'his son Avantivarman deposed Utpalapida and claimed the throne c. 855 with help from minister Sura'. Same land, same realm: the Kashmir dossier treats the change as a rename (rule 2).

land.text: Kashmir: Didda 'adopted a nephew, Samgrāmarāja ... to be her heir in Kashmir. From this decision arose the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir'

successors.note: Didda page; Utpala infobox Succeeded by: Lohara dynasty.

capitals.name: Avantipura (Avantipur)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Avantipur'; 'The cities of Avantipur (Awantipora) and Suyapur (Sopore) were founded during the reign' of Avantivarman. The page dates no move; 'Sugandha relocated to Haskapura' (undated, 904-906) is a refuge, not a new capital. Coordinates are those of the Kashmir dossier.

rulers.name: Avantivarman
rulers.note: Utpala table; infobox 'Established: 855'. The text: 'ascended to the throne in about 855/856, and went on to rule for 27 years until 883'.

rulers.name: Shankaravarman
rulers.note: 'died in 902 of a stray-arrow at a foreign territory'.

rulers.name: Chakravarman
rulers.note: The page also describes his death in 937; the table's 922-933 is used.

rulers.name: Chakravarman (3rd reign)
rulers.note: Utpala table: Chakravarman (3rd reign) 936-937; his one-year 2nd reign in 935 is folded into Shankaravardhana's line (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Yashaskara-deva
rulers.note: The table gives only 939 for Shuravarman II and Yashaskara; the end is Parvagupta's accession in 948.

rulers.name: Didda
rulers.title: Queen regnant
rulers.note: The table gives 980 to 1009/1012, the text c. 980-1003 and Samgramaraja succeeded her on 8 August 1003.

correction.text: Kashmir Valley and the Kashmir row's land of 850 (no Xinjiang, Ladakh or Baltistan), as in the kashmir dossier

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 855-859: Cliopatria's Utpala row begins in 960, 105 years after the page's 855. Avantivarman 'claimed the throne c. 855'; the page places only Valley towns in his reign (Avantipura, Surapura, Suyyapura) and says 'Rajatarangini records no military activity during his reign and frontier territories remained outside Kashmir sovereignty'. Drawn as the Kashmir dossier draws these years (its kashmir_850 correction): the Valley plus Cliopatria's Kashmir row of 850 without Xinjiang, Ladakh or Baltistan, so the two dossiers agree on the same land.

correction.text: Kashmir Valley and the Kashmir row's shape of 860-959 (no Xinjiang, Ladakh or Baltistan), as in the kashmir dossier

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 860-959: nothing in Cliopatria's Utpala row for these years. Drawn as the Kashmir dossier draws them (its kashmir_860 and kashmir_875 corrections, one outline): the Valley plus Cliopatria's Kashmir shape of 860-959 without Xinjiang, Ladakh or Baltistan; its Jammu and Himachal side stays at confidence 1 in that dossier because 'frontier territories remained outside Kashmir sovereignty' (Avantivarman) and the page names no land added later. Shankaravarman 'invaded Gujarat' and 'Alakhana, the local ruler had to gift a swath of territory' (883-902) and Gopalavarman led an expedition against a Hindu Shahi king of Udabhanda c. 903: neither land is named, so nothing is added.

correction.text: Kashmir Valley and the Kashmir row's shape of 960-1027 (no Xinjiang, Ladakh or Baltistan), as in the kashmir dossier

keyframe_review.note: 174,993 km2 (597 cells) for 960-961; the shape does not belong to the Utpala realm as the page gives it. It holds 7 of the 56 cells of the Kashmir Valley and none of Cliopatria's own Kashmir shape for 960 (0 of 370 cells): it is a ring around the Valley: Gilgit-Baltistan (Northern Areas) 226 of 226 cells, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 88, Xinjiang 77, Ladakh 58, Gorno-Badakhshan and Dushanbe regions of Tajikistan 58 each, Badakhshan (Afghanistan) 57, Jammu and Kashmir 15, Azad Kashmir 10. The two pages name only Valley places (Avantipura, Suyyapura (Sopore), Samkarapura (Pattan), Pandrethan, Padmapura (Pampore), Haskapura) and Lohara in the Pir Panjal (Didda's father's land); no page gives the Utpalas Gilgit, Chitral, Ladakh, Xinjiang or the Pamirs. Replaced by the land the Kashmir dossier draws for these years (its kashmir_960 correction).

174,396 km2 (597 cells) for 962-999: same ring, same verdict as 960; 7 of the 56 Valley cells. Didda (980-1003) 'Did not embark on any adventure involving a conflict with any neighboring ruler during her rule' (Didda page), and the page records no land won or lost in 962-999.

174,918 km2 (597 cells) for 1000-1002: same ring, same verdict as 960. 'Mahmud of Ghazni did not raid Kashmir as far as 1013'; 'Didda died in 1003, ten years before Mahmud of Ghazni invaded', so no war falls in these years.

New keyframe 1003-1003: Cliopatria's Utpala row ends in 1002 but Didda 'ruled as Queen regnant from 980 until her death in 1003' (8 August 1003) and the infobox says 'Disestablished: 1003'. The 960 correction is carried to the end of the year; Samgramaraja then founds the Lohara dynasty on the same land.

region.text: the Valley of Kashmir around Avantipur (Awantipora), Suyyapura (Sopore), Samkarapura (Pattan) and Padmapura (Pampore), the places the page names

ledger.note: 855: Avantivarman founds the Utpala dynasty in Kashmir. Infobox 'Established: 855'; 'Founded by Avantivarman in 855, it replaced the Karkota dynasty'; 'claimed the throne c. 855 with help from minister Sura'. Drawn on the Valley, where the page puts every town of the reign.

region.text: the Jammu and Himachal side of Cliopatria's 860 jump in the Kashmir row (Ladakh, Baltistan, Xinjiang and the Valley taken out)

ledger.note: 860 (bridge): the Jammu and Himachal side of Cliopatria's 860 jump in the Kashmir row (241 cells). Mirror of the same-year event in the kashmir dossier; the Utpala page records no conquest and says Avantivarman's reign had 'no military activity' with 'frontier territories ... outside Kashmir sovereignty', so the claim is confidence 1.

region.text: the Valley of Kashmir around Avantipur (Awantipora), Suyyapura (Sopore), Samkarapura (Pattan) and Padmapura (Pampore), the places the page names

ledger.note: 8 August 1003: Didda dies and the Utpala line ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1003'; Didda page: 'Reign: 980 - 8 August 1003'; she 'adopted a nephew, Samgrāmarāja, Udayaraja's eldest son to be her heir in Kashmir. From this decision arose the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir'. Land and rule continue under the Lohara dynasty (a rename in the kashmir dossier).

wars.name: Shankaravarman's invasion of Gujarat
wars.outcome: 'Kalhana notes that Sankaravarman invaded Gujarat with an army composed of nine lac infantrymen, three hundred elephants and one lac cavalry'; 'Alakhana, the local ruler had to gift a swath of territory to maintain his sovereignty'. Shankaravarman 'died in 902 of a stray-arrow at a foreign territory, whilst returning from a successful conquest'.
wars.note: The page dates the invasion nowhere inside the reign (table 883-902; infobox 885-902) and names no land of the swath, so no zone and no gain are recorded.

wars.name: Gopalavarman's expedition against Udabhanda
wars.outcome: 'Gopalavarman led a famed expedition against a rebel Hindu Shahi king of Udabhanda c. 903'. The page gives no result and no land.

wars.name: Tantrin and Damara revolts
wars.outcome: Partha 'was finally overthrown by the Tantrins' in 921; Chakravarman restored in 935 and had to flee again; 'their combined forces took on Sambhuvardhana in the spring of 936 near Padmapura' (Pampore); 'In the summer of 937, a group of Damara guards attacked Cakravarman'. The Utpala line itself ran on to 1003.
wars.note: A civil war inside the Valley; no border moved.

certainty.note: No treaty line or border appears on either page; only Valley towns and Lohara are named. The Valley is ringed by mountains; every outer limit is approximate.

notes:
Settled from the two pages (Utpala dynasty, Didda): founding 855 (Avantivarman, replacing the Karkotas), the capital Avantipur, the Valley towns of the reigns, the ruler table, Didda's death on 8 August 1003 and the Lohara succession.
Disagreements: (1) Shankaravarman reigns 883-902 in the table but 885-902 in the infobox. (2) Didda reigns 980 to 1009/1012 in the Utpala table but 'c. 980 - 1003' in its text and the Didda page ('980 - 8 August 1003'); 1003 is used (the infobox says Disestablished 1003). (3) The Utpala text says Chakravarman ruled 'till 933/934' yet fought and died in 936-937; the table's reigns are used with the later events listed in the war entry. (4) The Utpala text says 'This brought an end to the Utpala dynasty and would set the stage for Didda's autocracy' while the infobox runs to 1003 with Didda as the last ruler; 1003 is kept.
Not settled: the land of Shankaravarman's 'swath of territory' (the page names only 'Gujarat', no place a map can hold) and the land of the Udabhanda expedition; the extent of the realm in 860-1003 (no page names any place outside the Valley and Lohara). Cliopatria's Utpala row (597 cells in a ring of Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Xinjiang, Ladakh, the Pamirs and Badakhshan; 7 of 56 Valley cells; 0 of the 370 cells of its own Kashmir row of 960) is marked wrong and replaced by the land the Kashmir dossier draws; do not draw both rows.
ONE STATE: this row, karkota-dynasty and the Kashmir row are dynasties of one realm on the same land; the kashmir dossier carries the whole run 625-1339 with rename events (rule 2). This dossier mirrors its shapes and ruler strip exactly so that a merge loses nothing. The Ghazni attempts at Loharkot (1015, 1021) fall after 1003 and belong to the kashmir/lohara dossiers.
Pages: 2 (Utpala dynasty, Didda), the budget of 1-2.
